name: Achilles
hook: The Iliad's greatest warrior, invulnerable except for the heel that killed him.

facts.label: Thetis and the River Styx
facts.statement: His mother Thetis dipped the infant Achilles in the River Styx by the heel, leaving that spot vulnerable; the Achilles tendon still carries his name.

facts.label: the Iliad
facts.statement: Homer's Iliad is the Trojan War epic built on the wrath of Achilles, and it contains the duels of Menelaus and Paris and of Achilles and Hector.

facts.label: Hector
facts.statement: Hector is Troy's greatest warrior; he kills Achilles' friend Patroclus, and Achilles then kills Hector and drags his body around Patroclus' tomb.

facts.label: Paris
facts.statement: Paris, with Apollo's help, shoots the arrow into Achilles' heel that kills him; Paris is later killed by a poisoned arrow himself.

facts.label: Ajax
facts.statement: Ajax, son of Telamon, ranks second only to Achilles among the Greek heroes and recovers Achilles' body from the Trojans.

facts.label: Chiron
facts.statement: The centaur Chiron taught the young Achilles to play the lyre; he also taught Jason.

facts.label: Hephaestus
facts.statement: Hephaestus forged Achilles' armor, and W.H. Auden's poem 'The Shield of Achilles' calls the fire god 'the thin-lipped armorer.'
